## Match the Tool to the Question You're Asking

With this many tools available, the real skill isn't memorizing all of them — it's picking the right one fast, based on what you're actually trying to find out. This lesson is a decision guide, not new material.

## By Goal

| Your Goal | Reach For |
|---|---|
| Fast, broad first-pass scan of an unfamiliar model | Garak |
| Enterprise pipeline, multi-modal, chained multi-turn attacks | PyRIT |
| RAG chatbot — hallucination & factual consistency, not just jailbreaks | Giskard |
| Structured vulnerability × attack-strategy matrix for a compliance report | DeepTeam |
| Red teaming wired into CI/CD, no-code YAML config | Promptfoo |
| Target has a classic ML classifier (spam/fraud/moderation filter) | ART / CleverHans |
| Well-defended target resists off-the-shelf jailbreak libraries | PAIR / TAP / GCG |
| Target has a perplexity-based filter that flags unnatural text | AutoDAN |
| Need a defensible, benchmarked attack success number for a report | JailbreakBench / HarmBench |
| Attacking a classifier-based guardrail layer specifically | TextAttack |
| Understanding what a defense stack might look like before testing it | Rebuff |

## By Access Level

**Black-box (API access only, no weights):** Garak, Promptfoo, DeepTeam, PAIR, TAP, JailbreakBench — all designed to work purely through queries.

**White-box (model weights available):** GCG, AutoDAN, ART's gradient-based evasion attacks — these need internal access to compute gradients or run optimization directly against the model.

This maps directly onto the white-box vs black-box distinction from the AI Evasion module — the same access-level thinking applies here, just against generative models instead of classifiers.

## A Practical Engagement Flow

1. **Recon** — Nmap/service discovery to map the AI stack (model-serving port, vector DB, MCP servers)
2. **Broad scan** — Garak against the primary LLM endpoint for fast baseline coverage
3. **Targeted deep-dive** — pick DeepTeam or PyRIT based on whether you need matrix-style vulnerability coverage or chained multi-turn attacks
4. **RAG-specific testing** — Giskard if the target is knowledge-grounded
5. **Resistant findings** — escalate to PAIR/TAP/GCG for prompts that survive the broad scans
6. **Classifier layer (if present)** — ART/CleverHans/TextAttack against any guardrail or moderation model sitting in front of the LLM
7. **Report** — Promptfoo's HTML report or a JailbreakBench-style benchmark comparison for defensible, reproducible evidence

No single tool replaces understanding the attack. Every tool in this module automates something you already learned to do by hand in earlier modules — prompt injection, RAG poisoning, evasion, agent exploitation. If a tool's automated output doesn't make sense, go back to first principles rather than trusting the tool blindly; automated scanners produce false positives and false negatives just like any other scanner.
